text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia will be accepted to the European Union (EU) only around the year 2010, said Herbert Boesch, Chairman of the EU-Slovak parliamentary committee.

- The Slovak economy ministry said it had asked the World Trade Organisation to analyse a recent Czech measure requiring importers to deposit 20 percent of the value of imported goods on an interest-free account for 180 days. Slovakia considers the measure as another customs duty that will hurt Slovak exports to the Czech Republic.

- The Slovak government is expected to discuss the current situation of trade with the Czech Republic at its regular session on Tuesday. The economy ministry said the government did not plan any administrative counter-measures against the Czech move.
- The government is also expected to discuss imposing quotas on imports of soft drinks from the Czech Republic at its Tuesday session.

- About 60 percent of Slovaks would have taken part in a referendum on Slovakia's integration to the EU if the referendum had been held in March 1997, a public opinion poll said. Around 82 percent of those polled would have voted in favour of the membership.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak association of small agriculture entrepreneurs has called for the government to provide direct credits for the troubled agriculture sector instead of providing state guarantees for bank loans.

- The Czech Republic is expected to export around 800,000 hectolitres of beer to Slovakia this year. The Slovak ministry of agriculture has proposed imposing quotas on beer imports limiting them to some 540,000 hectolitres a year.

- The Slovak governemnt is expected to demand an earlier meeting of the Czech-Slovak custom union than the originally planned first half of June to address the current Czech administrative measures aimed at limiting imports.

PRAVDA - According to unofficial documents, the National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, last year approved 364 direct sales, of which 209 cases were sales of property and 155 cases were sales of shares. Revenues from the sell-offs totalled 16.4 billion, while the book value of sold companies was some 43.5 billion crowns.

- Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik has rejected accusation by the Czech foreign ministry of damaging Czech interests by raising problem of return of the Slovak gold from Prague to Bratislava during his talks with NATO representatives. Hamzik said the problem with gold was not a topic at the discussions.
